sources.title: ReWorld: Representation Learning for World Action Models

omissions: Version scope: the title page identifies arXiv:2606.27504v2 [cs.CV], 24 August 2026, submitted to IEEE TPAMI. Title and all eleven authors match the catalog. No earlier edition was supplied, so differences from v1 cannot be established; submission does not establish acceptance.
The catalog affiliation string includes an IEEE Publication Technology Department entry unsupported by the inspected author block; verified metadata includes only HUST and Xiaomi EV.
Text extraction does not reconstruct figure images; inspect the retained PDF for figures and equation/table layout.
The extraction limitation was addressed by visually inspecting PDF pp. 1–11, all five figures, all eight tables and every final crop.
Separate supplemental material availability has not been fully verified.
No separate supplement was supplied. Code was not inspected and experiments were not reproduced.

synopsis: ReWorld trains the internal connection between a video generator and a trajectory planner. It supervises intermediate video states, aligns action states with attended video information, then fine-tunes both networks using nearby low-scoring trajectories. Reported gains cover generated video, simulated driving and frozen action-recognition features. The strongest video result combines representation training with changed sampling; the driving result concerns non-reactive NAVSIM simulation.

problem.text: Exposing video features to a planner does not ensure they predict dynamics or remain useful after cross-attention. Expert imitation also weakly distinguishes geometrically similar trajectories with different safety outcomes. The authors call this a representation bottleneck and target the intermediate world-to-action pathway.

contributions.text: Three sequential objectives target representation formation, cross-modal retention and behavioral separation. Targets reuse video flow supervision, attended readouts and simulator-scored candidates; no external representation teacher is introduced.

Intermediate prediction also enables self-guided video sampling. Experiments cover video quality, planning, frozen representation transfer, controlled generative baselines and sensitivity to layer placement and regularization.

inputs: Camera history/video clips encoded by a spatiotemporal VAE
Ego kinematics and navigation command; motion-conditioned text through frozen T5 for the video branch
Noised video latents and normalized trajectories for flow training
Training-only experts and offline simulator-scored candidate trajectories
outputs: Future video through the Video DiT and decoder when requested
Ego trajectory of L waypoints (x, y, yaw) from the Action DiT

steps.name: Connect separate video and action generators
steps.detail: The backbone combines a 2B Video DiT and 133M Action DiT. Features F come from the first discrete video denoising step, at maximum noise. Cached means reused activations within the current graph across action-flow steps, not an offline feature database.

steps.name: Supervise the video interior
steps.detail: An auxiliary head at block 8 predicts the same noise-minus-clean-latent velocity target as the final head, directly constraining intermediate features. Training supervision and inference self-guidance are distinct mechanisms.

steps.name: Retain the attended world readout
steps.detail: At Action DiT cross-attention layer 12, cosine alignment compares post-attention states with stop-gradient attended video readouts. Video parameters are frozen, but readouts are recomputed and depend on current action-side attention weights.

steps.name: Repel nearby poor trajectories
steps.detail: Score 64 candidates per training scene offline with NAVSIM PDM. Among scores below 0.6, select the nearest to the expert in normalized waypoint space. Repel the clean trajectory estimate using negative mean absolute distance over normalized position increments and sine/cosine yaw. Expert flow matching anchors the prediction; invalid-negative scenes contribute no repulsion.

training.text: Video data use nuPlan/nuScenes at 8 Hz; NAVSIM supervision uses 2 Hz observations. Baseline pretraining progresses from 740×352×121 to 1280×704×25 clips. Stage 1 initializes from LTX-Video: 20k steps, batch 64, AdamW learning rate 10⁻⁵, weight decay 0.05.

Stage 2 freezes video parameters for 6k steps, batch 128, alignment weight 0.05. Stage 3 updates both branches for 10k steps, batch 160, repulsion weight 0.04; alignment is removed and online video features remain attached to action-loss gradients.

Checkpoint continuity is ambiguous: the method describes a progressive curriculum, but Section 4.1 says Stage 2 initializes from DriveLaW rather than explicitly from Stage 1. No undocumented checkpoint merge is assumed.

inference.text: Planning samples a Gaussian video latent, runs Video DiT once for F, then generates a trajectory in five action flow-matching steps without decoding future frames. Video generation separately uses 30 sampling steps and guidance scale 1.4. The reported method uses neither reinforcement learning nor test-time trajectory scoring.

The output is a plan evaluated in simulation. No physical actuator controller or on-road execution study is established; self-guidance refines video sampling without changing the first-step planner interface.

equations.explanation: Eqs. (1), (9): z₀ is the VAE-encoded clip, εz is Gaussian noise, and tv is video flow time. Final and intermediate heads regress this velocity target with squared error. Video and action flow times are independent.

equations.expression: \mathcal L_{\mathrm{Video}}=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{Gen}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{Mid}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{Mid}},\quad \mathcal L_{\mathrm{act}}^{(2)}=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{FM}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{align}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{align}},\quad \mathcal L_{\mathrm{act}}^{(3)}=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{FM}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{RDE}}\mathcal L_{\mathrm{RDE}}
equations.explanation: Eqs. (10), (14), (21): Gen/FM supervise video/expert-action flow; Mid supervises intermediate video prediction; align grounds action states; RDE repels a poor neighbor. Each λ weights its auxiliary term. Alignment and repulsion operate in different stages.
Eq. (11): vi and vf are intermediate and final predicted velocities; vw drives the sampling scheduler. Guidance strength γ=1 recovers the final prediction; the default is 1.4.

Eq. (18): action velocity vᵃφ converts the noised trajectory at time ta into an instantaneous clean estimate, conditioned on driving context ca and video features F. Denorm reverses normalization differentiably. Repulsion uses this same-pass estimate, not a separately sampled rollout.

results.setting: NAVSIM v1, approximately 12k Navtest scenes; camera-based methods on the same chained architecture; non-reactive simulation.
results.metric: PDMS ↑; NC, DAC, TTC, comfort, ego progress ↑
results.interpretation: A 1.3-point aggregate gain with slightly lower comfort; evidence concerns benchmark planning, not physical deployment.

results.task: Future video generation on nuScenes validation
results.setting: Table 1 validation protocol; intermediate supervision plus 30 sampling steps with γ=1.4.
results.comparison: DriveLaW 4.6/81.3; supervised ReWorld with γ=1 has FVD 78.9.
results.interpretation: The reported 23.9% relative FVD reduction combines training and inference changes. Video distribution scores do not measure executed driving.

results.task: Frozen action-recognition transfer on UCF-101 split 1
results.setting: 33-frame 224×224 clips; frozen final block of the 28-layer Video DiT, token mean pooling, common linear-classifier protocol.
results.interpretation: An 11.9 percentage-point gain over DriveLaW supports feature transfer, without isolating the cause of the later-stage gain.

results.setting: Separate 120k-step protocol: nuPlan/nuScenes, 224×224×25 clips, batch 32, no text encoder; nuScenes test FVD.
results.value: FVD 270.4; per-step video cost 1.003× at batch 1.
results.comparison: Vanilla Flow FVD 304.1 and cost 1.0×; Self-Flow FVD 283.3. Figure 2 reports roughly half the steps to comparable validation quality.
results.interpretation: This FVD protocol differs from Table 1. The 0.3% increment is video-side per-step cost, not total curriculum or mining cost.

results.setting: NAVSIM Navtest, same architecture; Stage 3 weight sweep starts from the best Stage 2 checkpoint.
results.value: Align only 89.5; RDE only 89.8; sequential ReWorld 90.4.
results.interpretation: The stages appear complementary; excessive repulsion competes with imitation. Table 7 checkmarks do not mean simultaneous losses.

limitations.text: NAVSIM is non-reactive and illustrated futures cover three seconds. Selected qualitative successes do not establish reactive traffic handling, calibrated physical dynamics or long-horizon reliability. The conclusion proposes longer horizons and multimodal extensions.

Reported tables omit seed variability and confidence intervals. Cross-paper comparisons differ in sensor inputs, and the controlled video protocol differs from the main one. Additional fine-tuning and freezing changes complicate causal attribution even within the same architecture.

RDE is unbounded below alone and is intended as a weak regularizer beside quadratic imitation. Table 8 shows weight sensitivity. Nearest-negative selection is motivated but not compared experimentally against random low-scoring negatives.

reproduction.text: Reproduction needs the specified backbones/data, train-only PDM candidate mining, identical normalization for mining and training, and the frozen probe protocol. A proposed first check holds checkpoints, validation clips, noises and sampling steps fixed while sweeping self-guidance.

Missing details include λMid, numerical trajectory length L and normalization constants, candidate guidance/noise scales, exact probe timestep/classifier schedule, and hardware/runtime. Resolve Stage 2 checkpoint provenance. A proposed second check compares nearest and random low-scoring negatives under equal fine-tuning budgets.

reasoning.text: Separate Video and Action DiTs support Dual-system despite joint Stage 3 gradients. IDM is plausible only as a broad latent-world-to-action label: the source specifies conditional trajectory flow from first-step video features, not an explicit inverse map from observed transitions or decoded futures. The architecture is supported, while the Q4 prediction paradigm remains unclear. Offline simulator-score mining is not reinforcement learning.

discussionQuestions: Would planning gains survive equal training budgets and identical checkpoint provenance?
Does nearest-negative mining beat random low-scoring negatives with matched score distributions?
Do feature gains predict performance in reactive traffic or longer planning horizons?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title/author/affiliation block, arXiv margin and abstract
evidence.detail: Title and eleven authors match; arXiv:2606.27504v2 is dated 24 Aug 2026, submitted to IEEE TPAMI. Affiliations are HUST and Xiaomi EV. Abstract states no RL or test-time scoring.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 1–2, Section 1, bottleneck and contributions
evidence.detail: Authors motivate future-predictive video features, retained attended information and distinction of nearby unsafe trajectories.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 3–4, Section 3.1, Eqs. (1)–(7); p. 2, Figure 1
evidence.detail: Separate 2B Video/133M Action DiTs use VAE/T5 and driving context. Action flow predicts normalized L×3 waypoints from first-step video features; planning uses one video pass without decoding future frames.
Block 8 uses the final flow target; self-guidance combines intermediate and final velocities only at sampling. FVD 61.9 includes both mechanisms.
Cosine alignment targets post-attention states at layer 12 with stop-gradient video readouts. Video parameters are frozen; attention-dependent targets are recomputed.

Hard negatives are nearest normalized candidates scoring below 0.6. RDE uses negative mean absolute delta-space distance on a clean estimate; empty valid sets give zero. Stage 3 jointly updates branches without alignment.

Specifies clip shapes, LTX initialization, 20k/6k/10k steps, 64/128/160 batches, optimizer, alignment 0.05, RDE 0.04, 64 candidates, 30 video/five action steps. Stage 2 explicitly starts from DriveLaW; several implementation constants are absent.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Section 4.1, tasks/datasets/metrics and Eq. (22)
evidence.detail: NAVSIM v1 is non-reactive, approximately 103k/12k train/test scenes. Video uses 8 Hz; trajectory observations 2 Hz. PDMS combines collision, drivable-area, progress, time-to-collision and comfort.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 1, DriveLaW/ReWorld rows; Section 4.2 video paragraph
evidence.detail: nuScenes validation FID/FVD: DriveLaW 4.6/81.3, ReWorld 4.4/61.9. Supervised ReWorld at γ=1 has FVD 78.9; reported full relative reduction is 23.9%.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Table 2, headers and DriveLaW/ReWorld rows
evidence.detail: Navtest PDMS 89.1 versus 90.4; NC/DAC/TTC/comfort/EP 99.0/97.1/96.7/100/81.3 versus 99.1/98.2/97.7/99.8/82.0. Sensor columns differ; dagger marks the same flow objective.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Table 3 and Section 4.3; p. 7, probing and Eq. (23)
evidence.detail: UCF-101 split 1 uses frozen final-block pooled features from 33-frame 224×224 clips: LTX 66.8%, DriveLaW 68.3%, Stage 1 71.7%, full ReWorld 80.2%.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Table 4; p. 7, unified protocol
evidence.detail: Separate 120k-step, batch-32, 224×224×25 no-text experiment reports nuScenes test FVD: Vanilla 304.1, Self-Flow 283.3, ReWorld 270.4.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Table 5, caption and ReWorld row
evidence.detail: Video-side per-step cost at 224×224×25 and batch 1: ReWorld 1.003× versus vanilla 1.0×.
Baseline/alignment-only/RDE-only/ReWorld yield Navtest PDMS 89.1/89.5/89.8/90.4. Alignment-only freezes video; the combined method is progressive.

evidence.location: PDF p. 11, Table 8(a)–(b) and caption; p. 10, Section 4.4
PDF p. 8, qualitative protocol; pp. 9–11, Figures 3–5 and captions
evidence.detail: Video examples show endpoints of one-second history and selected three-second future frames. Planning examples show red predictions and green experts for straight, left, right and intersection scenes.
Longer temporal horizons and multimodal scenarios are proposed as future work.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Figure 2(a)–(b) and caption; p. 9, Section 4.4
evidence.detail: The figure describes self-guidance and roughly twofold convergence acceleration at comparable validation FVD. The horizontal axis is optimization steps, not wall-clock time.
